questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The 39th Amendment, which placed the Prime Minister's election beyond judicial scrutiny, was struck down in:

options.A: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975)
options.B: I.C. Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967)
options.C: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)
options.D: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

questions.explanation: The Court held that free and fair elections form part of the basic structure.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 311(2), a civil servant cannot be dismissed or removed without:

options.A: A reasonable opportunity of being heard
options.B: A vote in the State Legislature
options.C: A recommendation from the High Court
options.D: The consent of the State Governor

questions.explanation: An inquiry in which he is informed of the charges and given a chance to defend is required.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In State of West Bengal v. Anwar Ali Sarkar, a law giving the Government unguided discretion to send cases to special courts was struck down under:
questions.explanation: The Court held that the classification was not based on any intelligible differentia.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India (2016), the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of:

options.B: Unnatural offences under Section 377 of the IPC
options.C: Adultery under Section 497 of the IPC
options.D: Sedition under Section 124A of the IPC

questions.explanation: Reputation was held to be part of the right to life under Article 21 and the restriction to be reasonable.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Disputes between the Union and one or more States fall within the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under:
questions.explanation: The jurisdiction is exclusive and extends to disputes involving a question of law or fact on which a legal right depends.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Special leave to appeal to the Supreme Court from any court or tribunal in India is granted under:
questions.explanation: Article 136 is discretionary and is exercised sparingly.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for:

options.A: Amending the Constitution of India in part
options.B: Dissolving a State Legislature before term
options.C: Doing complete justice in a pending matter
options.D: Dismissing the Council of Ministers at will

questions.explanation: The power cannot be used to override express statutory provisions.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 227 gives each High Court the power of superintendence over:

options.A: All courts and tribunals within its territory
options.B: Only courts of civil jurisdiction and appeal
options.C: Only courts in the State capital
options.D: Only the district courts within its own State

questions.explanation: L. Chandra Kumar held this power to be part of the basic structure.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 provides for reservation of one-third of seats for women in:

options.C: The Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils
options.D: The Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies

questions.explanation: The reservation will come into effect after the next delimitation exercise.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The total number of Ministers in a State Council of Ministers cannot exceed what proportion of the strength of the Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: The 91st Amendment inserted Article 164(1A); a State must have at least twelve Ministers.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The Ninth Schedule and Article 15(4) were added to the Constitution by the:
questions.explanation: The First Amendment followed the decision in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In the Aadhaar judgment (Puttaswamy, 2018), the Supreme Court struck down:

options.A: The whole of the Aadhaar Act
options.B: Section 139AA of the Income Tax Act

questions.explanation: The majority upheld the Aadhaar Act as a Money Bill and limited its use for private contracts.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Kaushal Kishore v. State of U.P. (2023), the Supreme Court held that the grounds in Article 19(2) are:

options.B: Illustrative only, so courts may add other grounds

questions.explanation: The Court also held that Fundamental Rights such as Articles 19 and 21 can be enforced against private persons in appropriate cases.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: In Dicey's view, the 'rule of law' means the absence of:

options.A: Ordinary law courts in the country

questions.explanation: Dicey stressed supremacy of regular law as opposed to wide discretionary authority.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The doctrine of separation of powers was elaborated by Montesquieu in:
questions.explanation: Montesquieu argued that liberty requires legislative, executive and judicial powers to be separate.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Hobbes, in Leviathan, argued that life in the state of nature is:

options.A: Governed by natural equality and justice
options.C: Solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short
options.D: Free from all fear and scarcity

questions.explanation: People therefore enter a social contract and submit to a sovereign.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: A decision rendered 'per incuriam' is one given:

options.C: By a full Bench of the court
options.D: After full hearing of both parties

questions.explanation: Such a decision does not have binding force as precedent.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: In The Republic, justice for Plato consists in:

options.B: Equal distribution of wealth to all citizens
options.C: Obedience to the will of the majority
options.D: Each class performing its proper function

questions.explanation: Plato's just State has rulers, auxiliaries and producers, each doing its own work.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Decisions of a High Court of another State are, for a High Court, only:
questions.explanation: Only decisions of the Supreme Court bind all courts under Article 141.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Rudolf Stammler is associated with the idea of:

options.B: Law as the command of the sovereign
options.C: Natural law with a variable content

questions.explanation: Stammler proposed 'natural law with changing content' guided by the social ideal of a community of free-willing people.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: In Central Inland Water Transport Corporation v. Brojo Nath Ganguly, a clause permitting termination of employment on notice was held:

options.A: A valid exercise of freedom of contract

questions.explanation: The Court applied the doctrine of unequal bargaining power to a standard form of employment contract.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 28 of the Contract Act, an agreement absolutely restraining a party from enforcing his rights through ordinary legal proceedings is:
questions.explanation: Arbitration agreements and agreements fixing limitation on rights to sue are saved in certain circumstances.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 29 of the Contract Act, an agreement whose meaning is not certain or capable of being made certain is:
questions.explanation: Uncertainty of terms renders the agreement void.

questions.subject: Specific Relief
questions.question: Under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, a person dispossessed of immovable property without consent may sue for recovery within:
questions.explanation: The suit is summary in nature, and no appeal lies from the decree, though a suit on title can follow.

questions.subject: Specific Relief
questions.question: A perpetual injunction under Section 38 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 is granted:

options.A: At any stage on an oral request by a party
options.C: By a decree made at the hearing on the merits
options.D: Only by the Registrar of the court in chambers

questions.explanation: A temporary injunction, in contrast, continues until a stated time or further orders.

questions.subject: Sale of Goods
questions.question: Under Section 19 of the Sale of Goods Act, in a contract for specific or ascertained goods, the intention as to when property passes is found from:

options.B: The seller's own declaration to the buyer alone
options.D: The contract terms, conduct and circumstances

questions.explanation: The intention of the parties governs, subject to the rules in Sections 20 to 24.

questions.subject: Sale of Goods
questions.question: Under Section 24 of the Sale of Goods Act, goods delivered 'on approval' become the buyer's when he:

options.A: Transports them to his own home
options.B: Pays a deposit to the seller
options.C: Signifies approval or keeps them too long
options.D: Inspects them once at the shop

questions.explanation: Property passes also when he retains the goods beyond the fixed or a reasonable time without giving notice of rejection.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha, the Supreme Court held that medical services rendered for consideration come within the:
questions.explanation: Services rendered free of charge are excluded, but those under contract of personal service are also excluded.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The maxim 'actio personalis moritur cum persona' means that:

options.A: A personal action dies with the person
options.B: Every action must be a personal one
options.D: A right of action passes to the State

questions.explanation: In India, the rule has been modified by statute, so that claims for property damage survive.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In Vaughan v. Taff Vale Railway Co., the railway company was not liable for fire from its engine because it acted under:
questions.explanation: Statutory authority is a defence where all reasonable care was taken to avoid damage.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In Cope v. Sharpe, the defence of necessity was held to apply to:

options.A: Murder to save one's own life

questions.explanation: A gamekeeper's entry on land to stop a fire spreading was justified.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Wilkinson v. Downton established liability for:
questions.explanation: A practical joke causing severe emotional distress to the plaintiff gave rise to damages.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Under the 'eggshell skull' rule, a defendant must take the plaintiff:

options.B: Only if he is of ordinary health
options.D: As the law presumes him to be

questions.explanation: The defendant is liable for the full extent of the harm even if the plaintiff was unusually vulnerable.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Waging war against the Government of India is punishable under which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 147 corresponds to Section 121 IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended in 2018), giving a bribe to a public servant is:

options.A: An offence only for public servants

questions.explanation: The 2018 amendment made bribe-giving a specific offence, with exceptions for coerced givers who report promptly.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Under Section 37 of the NDPS Act, bail for specified offences requires the court to be satisfied that the accused is:

options.A: Not guilty and unlikely to reoffend

questions.explanation: The Public Prosecutor must also be given an opportunity to oppose the bail application.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Section 29 of the POCSO Act, 2012 raises a presumption that the accused:

options.A: Is innocent until the victim testifies in court
options.D: Has committed the offence unless disproved

questions.explanation: The presumption applies to offences under Sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of the Act.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Under Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, giving or taking dowry carries a minimum imprisonment of:
questions.explanation: The minimum fine is ₹15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: In Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India (2022), the Supreme Court:

options.A: Struck down the entire PMLA as unconstitutional
options.B: Held PMLA to be a Money Bill only
options.C: Banned the ED from summoning accused persons
options.D: Upheld arrest powers and twin bail conditions

questions.explanation: The Court upheld Sections 19 and 45 of the PMLA.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, an aggrieved woman has the right to:
questions.explanation: Section 17 gives the right to reside in the shared household whether or not she has title.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Section 18 of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act bars:
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court in Prathvi Raj Chauhan (2020) upheld the bar, subject to a prima facie case.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: In Lalita Kumari v. Government of U.P., the Supreme Court held that registration of an FIR is mandatory where information discloses:
questions.explanation: A preliminary inquiry is permissible only in certain categories such as matrimonial or commercial disputes.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: In Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab, the Supreme Court held that anticipatory bail is:

options.B: Not limited to a fixed period
options.C: Restricted to offences under the IPC only

questions.explanation: The Constitution Bench rejected a rigid time-limit and left the matter to the court's discretion.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Confessions and statements recorded by a Magistrate during investigation are provided for in Section:
questions.explanation: Section 183 BNSS corresponds to Section 164 CrPC.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A statement made to the police during investigation can ordinarily be used at trial only to:
questions.explanation: Section 180 BNSS (earlier Section 161 CrPC) bars its use as substantive evidence except as provided.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: The power to examine the accused to explain the circumstances appearing against him in the evidence is in Section:
questions.explanation: Section 351 BNSS corresponds to Section 313 CrPC.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: The limitation period for a suit for specific performance of a contract under the Limitation Act, 1963 is:
questions.explanation: Article 54 prescribes three years from the date fixed for performance or from refusal.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 allows a party to seek from the court:

options.C: A final decree on the merits

questions.explanation: A party can apply before, during or after arbitral proceedings but before enforcement of the award.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Order II Rule 2 of the CPC requires the plaintiff to:

options.A: Claim all reliefs from one cause of action
options.B: File only one prayer in each suit
options.C: Sue only in the capital city

questions.explanation: A relief omitted intentionally cannot be claimed in a later suit on the same cause of action.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: In Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra, the Supreme Court laid down tests for conviction based on:
questions.explanation: The five 'golden principles' require that the circumstances form a complete chain pointing only to the guilt of the accused.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 154 of the Evidence Act, the court may permit a party to cross-examine his own witness who is:
questions.explanation: The court's permission is required.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 165 of the Evidence Act, a Judge may put questions to a witness:

options.C: At any time, to discover relevant facts
options.D: Only after the arguments are heard

questions.explanation: The Judge cannot, however, compel a witness to answer questions that he may lawfully refuse.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: A test identification parade is held to:

options.A: Prove the guilt of the accused
options.B: Test a witness's ability to identify the accused
options.C: Record a confession by the accused
options.D: Obtain a medical report on the accused

questions.explanation: It is a measure of investigation and is not substantive evidence by itself.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The UN Charter establishes how many principal organs?
questions.explanation: They are the General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ and the Secretariat.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Article 2(4) of the UN Charter prohibits:

options.A: The threat or use of force against another State
options.B: Membership of more than one organisation
options.C: Recognition of newly formed States by others
options.D: Trade between States that are in a dispute

questions.explanation: The prohibition is subject to self-defence and Security Council authorisation.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Enforcement action in response to threats to the peace is provided in which Chapter of the UN Charter?
questions.explanation: Chapter VII authorises the Security Council to take measures including sanctions and force.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court entered into force in:
questions.explanation: The Statute was adopted in 1998; India is not a party.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The Paris Agreement, 2015 aims to limit the global temperature rise to well below:
questions.explanation: It also pursues efforts to limit the increase to 1.5°C.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The right of peoples to self-determination is affirmed in Article 1(2) of the:
questions.explanation: It is also in Article 1 of the ICCPR and ICESCR.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 23 of the Registration Act, 1908, a document must ordinarily be presented for registration within:
questions.explanation: A further period of four months is allowed on payment of a fine.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 15 of the Indian Easements Act, an easement is acquired by prescription after uninterrupted enjoyment for:
questions.explanation: The enjoyment must be peaceable, open and as of right.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: A 'trust' under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 arises out of:

options.A: Confidence accepted by the owner of property
options.B: A statute of the State alone
options.C: A custom of the community alone
options.D: A decree of the High Court alone

questions.explanation: A trust is an obligation annexed to ownership and accepted by the owner for the benefit of another.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: In Muslim law, a gift of property made during the donor's lifetime is called:
questions.explanation: Wasiyat is a bequest operating after death; waqf is a dedication to God.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under the Mitakshara law, a son acquires a right in ancestral property:
questions.explanation: Under the 2005 amendment, daughters also have the same right by birth.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under Section 18 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, a Hindu wife is entitled to maintenance from her husband:

options.A: Only for five years after separation
options.B: For life, unless she is disqualified
options.C: Only on a court order every year
options.D: Only if she has no children

questions.explanation: She loses the right if she ceases to be a Hindu, is unchaste or lives separately without justification.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: The TRIPS Agreement, administered by the WTO, came into effect in:
questions.explanation: TRIPS sets minimum standards for IPR protection of WTO members.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: The Berne Convention, 1886 deals with the protection of:
questions.explanation: The Convention is administered by WIPO.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001 allows farmers to:

options.A: Save and sell farm-saved seed, except branded
options.B: Sell only to the Government at a fixed price
options.C: Import seeds without any quarantine control

questions.explanation: The Act protects breeders' and farmers' rights.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 3(j) of the Patents Act, 1970, which of the following is not patentable?
questions.explanation: Micro-organisms and non-biological and microbiological processes are not excluded.

questions.subject: Commercial Law
questions.question: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 replaced the:
questions.explanation: FEMA moved from a criminal regime to a civil one for most violations.

questions.subject: Maritime Law
questions.question: Under the Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017, admiralty jurisdiction is vested in:

options.A: Only the Supreme Court of India
options.D: The High Courts of coastal States

questions.explanation: The Act gives High Courts admiralty jurisdiction over maritime claims within their territorial limits.

questions.subject: Competition Law
questions.question: The CCI can penalise a cartel up to:

options.A: Ten lakh rupees only per violation
options.B: Thrice profit or 10% of turnover, if higher
options.C: Fifty per cent of the company's assets
options.D: One year's salary of all its directors

questions.explanation: Penalty under Section 27 of the Competition Act is calculated for each year of the cartel's continuance.

questions.subject: Insolvency Law
questions.question: Under the IBC, 2016, the moratorium under Section 14 prohibits:

options.A: Filing of tax returns by the debtor
options.B: Sale of the debtor's goods in ordinary course
options.D: Suits and recovery actions against the debtor

questions.explanation: The moratorium protects the corporate debtor from claims during the insolvency resolution process.

questions.subject: Consumer Law
questions.question: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the CCPA can order:

options.A: Transfer of all consumer disputes to foreign courts
options.D: Recall of unsafe goods and refund of prices

questions.explanation: The Authority can also impose penalties for misleading advertisements.

questions.subject: Right to Information
questions.question: Under Section 19 of the RTI Act, the first appeal lies to:

options.A: The High Court of the concerned State
options.B: A senior officer in the authority
options.C: The Lokpal of India as first appeal
options.D: The Supreme Court of India directly

questions.explanation: A second appeal lies to the Information Commission.
